descriptionChirho: The proper noun תַּחְפַּנְחֵס / תְּהַפְנְחֵס referring to Tahpanhes (Daphne), an Egyptian border city in the eastern Nile Delta where Judean refugees fled after the fall of Jerusalem (Jeremiah 2:16, 43:7-9, 44:1, 46:14; Ezekiel 30:18). All three clusters represent the same place name in different syntactic and orthographic forms: S144978 (5x, with prepositions 'in Tahpanhes'), S144981 (2x, conjunctive 'and-Tahpanhes' with ketiv/qere variation), and S144980 (1x, variant spelling Tehaphnehes). Multilingual evidence is consistent: Spanish Tajpanjés/Tajpanjes/Tahpanhes, Arabic تحفنحيس uniformly, Hindi तखपनहेस/तहपन्हेस, Korean 다후네스/답팁헤스 (transliteration variants), Swahili Tahpanesi/Tehafnehesi. The orthographic variations are scribal, not semantic.
